import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    ids = list(feats.ids)
    types = list(feats.types)
    corr_pairs = [(a,b) for a,b in [
        ('AZI11','RDD4B'), ('XDEH17B','ZKH7'), ('NWL9L','RDD4B'), 
        ('RDD4B','OWGI5B'), ('NWL9L','AZI11'), ('AZI11','OWGI5B'),
        ('XRNT16A','RDD4B'), ('CQKW2','RDD4B'), ('NWL9L','OWGI5B'),
        ('GDBP17','VEU12L'), ('GDBP17','RKV5L'), ('AZI11','CQKW2'),
        ('GDBP17','RDD4B'), ('RLLI19','EXE1L'), ('GWV10','RDD4B'),
        ('BGUV7','BBXR10'), ('XRNT16A','OWGI5B'), ('CQKW2','OWGI5B'),
        ('JCB1A','QUZO2P'), ('CQKW2','QUZO2P')
    ] if a in ids and b in ids]
    
    # Keep one feature from each highly correlated pair
    keep = set(ids)
    for a,b in corr_pairs:
        if a in keep and b in keep:
            # Prefer the one with higher t-statistic
            idx_a = ids.index(a)
            idx_b = ids.index(b)
            ta = feats.x[:,idx_a].std() * (feats.x[feats.y==1,idx_a].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0,idx_a].mean())
            tb = feats.x[:,idx_b].std() * (feats.x[feats.y==1,idx_b].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0,idx_b].mean())
            if abs(ta) < abs(tb):
                keep.remove(a)
            else:
                keep.remove(b)
    
    # Filter to keep only non-duplicate features
    keep_ids = [id for id in ids if id in keep]
    keep_idx = [i for i, id in enumerate(ids) if id in keep]
    
    # Compute effect sizes (difference in means)
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(keep_ids):
        col = feats.column(fid)
        effect = feats.x[feats.y==1,col].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0,col].mean()
        effects.append((abs(effect), fid, i))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top drivers (at most MAX_DRIVERS)
    drivers = tuple(fid for _, fid, _ in effects[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # For logistic regression, include all features with significant effects
    columns = tuple(fid for _, fid, _ in effects if abs(_) > 0.1)
    
    # Check for potential interactions between top features
    products = []
    for i, (eff1, f1, _) in enumerate(effects[:3]):
        for j, (eff2, f2, _) in enumerate(effects[:3]):
            if i < j:
                products.append((f1, f2))
    
    # Simple weighted score: sum of top features
    loadings = {}
    for eff, fid, _ in effects[:3]:
        loadings[fid] = eff
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
